sources.entry: Browser Cookie Bridge - Transfer signed-in sessions between local Chromium browsers and ChatGPT Codex on macOS.

summary.one_liner: A macOS app (SwiftUI, menu-bar helper) that copies signed-in browser cookie sessions between local Chromium browsers, into ChatGPT Codex or Cursor's built-in browser, into an encrypted Grok Bot transfer file, or optionally to a Browserless Cloud authenticated profile.
summary.what_it_does: Reads cookies from a selected local Chromium-based browser (Brave, Chrome, Edge, Arc, Vivaldi, Opera, or Perplexity Comet) and writes them to another supported endpoint. Browser-to-browser transfers use small unpacked extensions and a short-lived loopback broker. For ChatGPT Codex and experimental Cursor, it merges cookies into the app's embedded browser database after making a backup and validating the result. For Grok Bot, it writes an AES-256-GCM encrypted .bcbx bundle that embeds its decryption key. Optional features include history URLs and full site data for Codex, scheduled or login-time sync, a Browserless cloud upload with size preflight and post-upload verification, and built-in GitHub release updates. Cookie values are stated to never be logged.
use_cases: Move logged-in sessions from Chrome or Brave into ChatGPT Codex on a Mac
Sign into the Cursor browser using cookies from another browser
Create an encrypted cookie transfer file for a Grok Bot cloud browser
Upload authenticated browser profile state to Browserless Cloud
Avoid re-logging into the same websites across several Chromium browsers
Automate daily or login-time cookie syncing between local browser profiles
notable: Grok Bot .bcbx export: encrypted bundle with embedded decryption key and a bundled importer, so no passphrase is needed on import
Backs up the destination app's browser database, modifies a copy, integrity-checks it, and restores on failure
Browserless uploads are manual, token stored in macOS Keychain, and the app reports omitted origins when the 2 MB artifact limit is hit
Local-first: no account, analytics, or remote relay for local transfers
Cursor import writes only to its dedicated partition and refuses unknown schemas
caveats: macOS only (macOS 13.5+); a Windows app is only being explored, with a waitlist
Cursor import is experimental and cookies-only; Cursor is destination-only
Direct imports store cookie values in plaintext SQLite columns, readable by software running as the same macOS user
Grok Bot .bcbx files contain the decryption key, so they must be treated as credentials
Browserless currently caps the serialized profile at 2 MB, so large site data may be dropped
